items.claim: Test for stack-less original error now passes an error that has a stack
items.consequence: The test named 'creates new stack if original error has no stack' no longer exercises that case, so a regression in the fallback goes green. Its fixture changed from the stack-less `{ message: 'original' }` to `new Error('original')`, which always carries a stack, so the constructor takes the reuse-the-original-stack branch (GraphQLError.js:195) and the only stack assertion, `to.be.a('string')`, passes trivially; the test is now a weaker duplicate of 'uses the stack of an original error' and no test passes a stack-less originalError. For example, simplifying the guard to `if (originalError)` would leave `e.stack` undefined for stack-less originals while the suite stays green. Restoring a stack-less fixture restores the guard without giving up Flow coverage.
items.proposed_fix: Make the fixture stack-less again so the fallback branch is exercised. Either keep the real Error and remove its stack (`const original = new Error('original'); delete original.stack;` - confirmed at runtime by a scratch mocha probe to leave `original.stack` undefined and make the constructor capture a new stack; not checked under Flow), or restore the object fixture behind a cast (`const original: any = { message: 'original' };`, the same `any` device this diff uses at src/error/__tests__/locatedError-test.js:30). Optionally assert `expect(original.stack).to.equal(undefined)` so the precondition cannot silently drift again.

items.claim: Constructor declaration accepts null nodes; implementation signature does not
items.consequence: Callers are now told they may pass `null` for `nodes`, but the function that actually runs is still type-checked as if `null` could never arrive. Only the `declare class` signature was widened; the implementation a few lines below keeps `| void` without `| null`, so Flow checks the body against a narrower type than callers can supply. Today the body handles null correctly, so nothing breaks; the cost is that a later edit to the body which distinguishes undefined from other values would type-check and still mishandle the null the declaration invites. Widening the implementation parameter to match is a one-token change that keeps the two signatures in the same file honest with each other.
items.proposed_fix: Give the implementation the same parameter type as the declaration: change src/error/GraphQLError.js:94 to `nodes?: $ReadOnlyArray<ASTNode> | ASTNode | void | null,`. The body already treats null like undefined (`: nodes ? [nodes] : undefined`), so no logic change is needed. Assumes Flow accepts the widened parameter in the body; `flow check` was not run in this review.

native_payload.intent: Enable Flow type checking on the error-module tests and the `inspect` test by replacing `@noflow` with `@flow strict`, adjusting the tests only as far as needed to type-check (shared parsed fixture, `invariant` narrowing, `any` casts, one `$FlowFixMe`). Widen the Flow declaration of the `GraphQLError` constructor so `nodes` also accepts `null`. No runtime behavior change is intended, and every touched test must keep guarding the behavior its name claims.

residual_risks: Flow was not run by either read (`flow check` is outside this review's execution allowance), so the change's central claim - that the four test files type-check under `@flow strict` with flow-bin 0.86 and that the widened constructor declaration is accepted - is unverified here. That includes whether the new `// $FlowFixMe` at src/jsutils/__tests__/inspect-test.js:31 on the `String.raw` line is still needed (reported by: correctness, adversarial).
